question.prompt: On grid paper, \(l\) is a vertical line. Points \(A\) and \(B\) lie on the same horizontal line, on the left and right sides of \(l\), respectively. The distance from \(A\) to \(l\) is 3 squares, and the distance from \(B\) to \(l\) is 2 squares. Points \(A'\) and \(B'\) are the reflections of \(A\) and \(B\) across \(l\), respectively. Find the length of \(A'B'\). (Unit: grid squares)

solutions.explanation: After reflection, \(A'\) is 3 squares to the right of \(l\), and \(B'\) is 2 squares to the left of \(l\). They remain on the same horizontal line, so \(A'B'=3+2=5\) (equal to \(AB\)).
solutions.title: Locate the reflected points

solutions.explanation:
Reflection preserves segment lengths, so we can find \(AB\) without locating the reflected points. Because \(A\) and \(B\) lie on the same horizontal line on opposite sides of the vertical line \(l\), their perpendicular distances to \(l\) form the two parts of \(AB\). Therefore,
\[
A'B'=AB=3+2=5.
\]
The length is \(5\) grid squares.
solutions.title: Use preservation of length
